solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fine-looking year ahead

definitions.meaning: describing perfect eyesight, the standard score on an optician's chart
the year then still to come when the puzzle appeared in 2017

explanation.surface: A forecast that the coming year will look good.
explanation.walkthrough: Perfect vision is scored as a fraction on the eye chart, written with the same number twice; that same pair read as a year was three years off.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal sharp eyesight is described by this chart fraction, and the calendar year 2020 lay ahead.

clue.text: From the 11: double 4, then bullseye and … one hundred and eighty!

indicators.note: then sets the bullseye word after the darts nickname

parts.note: 4 across is the top number on a dartboard, and players nickname its double ring 'tops'
the core is the centre, as the bullseye is the centre of a target

explanation.surface: A darts commentator calling a throw from the oche, ending in a maximum.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubles plus bullseye cannot add to 180; the numbers are a false trail. The 11 is OCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Three treble twenties make 180, the maximum possible from three darts.

clue.text: 'E', I think, winds up 'effuse'

indicators.note: in a down entry, winds up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: 'to me' means in my opinion, as I think

explanation.surface: Someone commenting that the letter E ends up as effuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds up' reverses E + TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To effuse is to pour out feeling, and to emote is to show emotion theatrically.

clue.text: Like 1ac and 4, you'll find it in dartboard

indicators.note: with 'in', this says the abbreviation is found within the word for the puzzle's subject
with 'you'll find', this places the sex appeal letters inside

parts.note: the dartboard is this puzzle's theme
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A darts fact about two numbers on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' = SA is old slang for sex appeal; the setter treats the dartboard as THEME, the puzzle's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Entries 1 and 4 are identical words, so they are identical to each other.

clue.text: See 1
Endless blitzing of 25 he thwarted?

indicators.note: the 'he' cuts across the scrambled letters, sitting inside them
a blitz smashes things apart, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: 25 across is ARROWS, darts

explanation.surface: A man who stopped endless bombing raids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blitzing of' rearranges the shortened ARROW to WARRO. 25 is the darts slang entry; read whole, the clue describes someone who beat the Blitz.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who thwarted a bombing campaign would be celebrated as a decorated military champion.

clue.text: The setter's pa joins grandma climbing mountain

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing reads the pieces from the bottom up

parts.note: the setter has, from the setter's own view, is I've
dad is an informal word for father, as pa is
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A family outing where the setter's father and grandmother climb a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is 'the setter has', I'VE; the pieces reverse in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanda Devi is one of India's highest Himalayan peaks, in Uttarakhand.

clue.text: The Jester I see put down as entry for Ebor

indicators.note: the letters are written in as an insertion into the city name

parts.note: Ebor is the old name for York, from Latin Eboracum, used by its archbishops
the letter C is spoken just like 'see'

explanation.surface: A racegoer writing down a horse named The Jester for York's Ebor race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ebor is a famous horse race at York, so 'entry' looks racing; Ebor itself is York.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet holds the skull of the dead court jester, the king's fool, in the graveyard scene.

clue.text: Covering pages one and two regularly irritated rival

indicators.note: the scrambled letters wrap around the abbreviation for pages, covering it
irritated suggests stirred up, so the letters are rearranged
every other letter of 'and two' is taken, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by a rival who read pages one and two over their shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges the six letters to OONENT; 'Covering' wraps them round the pages abbreviation, which lands after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival is the person you play against, a direct synonym for an opposing competitor.

clue.text: The sort of guy who compiles crosswords? Ralph may make it difficult

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
what a crossword setter does is setting

explanation.surface: A dig at crossword setters, with someone called Ralph making life hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralph is old printers' slang for the imp blamed for errors in the composing room.
explanation.definitionFit: Composing printed pages letter by letter was the trade where the mischievous sprite was said to cause mistakes.

clue.text: Across verges of rockery river stopped flowing

indicators.note: the verges are laid across the abbreviation for river, so it sits inside them

parts.note: the verges, or edges, of the word rockery are R and Y, read literally with the 'and'
R is the usual map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Water in a garden rockery feature has dried up at its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The verges of 'rockery' are 'R and Y' spelt out in full, giving RANDY; 'Across' puts that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream that has run out of water has ceased to flow, the idiom for exhausted supply.

clue.text: Line of 25 flipping hot green bottles!

indicators.note: bottles here is a verb, holding the letter for hot inside
flipping turns the word for green over so it reads backwards

parts.note: eco, as in eco-friendly, means environmentally green
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A line of darts players getting heated about green bottles in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses ECO to OCE; 'bottles' puts H inside. 25 is ARROWS, slang for darts.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the oche is the mark on the floor behind which a thrower must stand.

clue.text: Device Ian's submitting to Jacob's brother's relish

indicators.note: Ian yields his place to the brother, so those letters are swapped out for the brother's name

parts.note: an appliance is a household device
the name taken as written
Esau is Jacob's twin brother in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man named Ian handing over his sauce to Jacob's biblical brother.
explanation.walkthrough: In APPLIANCE the letters IAN are replaced by ESAU; the final 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit sauce served with pork is a condiment, which is what a relish is.

clue.text: After two interruptions, what is 144 for one?

definitions.text: After two interruptions, what is 144 for one?

parts.words: After two interruptions, what is 144 for one?
parts.note: split 144 twice to get 1, 4, 4: entries 1 and 4 name the short format of the game, and '4 for one' is the number from entry 4 with one wicket down, a typical tally in that format

explanation.surface: A riddle about breaking up a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 144 for one is itself a plausible innings total; broken into 1-4-4 it reads as the T20 format followed by a score of the 4 entry for one wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs for wickets lost is how a batting side's tally is written in the bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Buffet measuring meat served up in carriage?

indicators.note: the measuring word and reversed meat go in the carriage

parts.note: a car is a carriage, as on a train
of, as in 'a rod of two metres', means measuring

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means read upwards

parts.note: beef is a meat

explanation.surface: A train buffet car serving measured portions of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses BEEF to FEEB.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a counter selling snacks and drinks, as a café-style snack counter does.

clue.text: Overtures from Wagner which blues duo restyled?

definitions.note: the opening letters of 'Wagner' and 'which' are a pair of W letters

indicators.note: restyled means given a new form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A blues duo reworking Wagner's overtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overtures' means the first letters, W and W, not the operatic pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Two W letters, each named as the letter after V, said as a pair.

clue.text: High-up intent on firing her, tip failing to charge new format for Flog It!

indicators.note: to charge a gun is to load it, so the shuffled letters are packed inside
a new format reshapes the title's letters

parts.note: the title of a BBC antiques-selling television show, taken letter by letter

indicators.note: failing means the letters of 'her tip' collapse into disorder

explanation.surface: A TV executive revamping the antiques show Flog It! and sacking a presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-up' looks like a senior executive, but it is an airman. 'to charge' means load, as with a gun: one scrambled set is packed inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman flying a combat jet is literally high up and there to shoot, a cryptic description.

clue.text: With no initial form run announced horse in nursery stakes? Super!

indicators.note: stakes here means encloses, as a stake fence surrounds

parts.note: go means run, as a machine does

indicators.note: the nursery horse word is said out loud as two letters

parts.note: gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: mode means form or manner

explanation.surface: A racing tip about a nursery stakes, a race for two-year-olds.
explanation.walkthrough: A nursery stakes is a race for young horses. Gee-gee said aloud spells GG.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a decent sort, thoroughly nice, is an old-fashioned exclamation of approval.

clue.text: Brute came to us by boat, caught from Billingsgate?

indicators.note: as heard in the London fish market, in a Cockney accent that drops its H

parts.note: rowed here: arrived at this spot by rowing a boat

explanation.surface: A brute arriving by boat at a fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's fish market, a byword for Cockney speech, which drops the H of 'here'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a dumb beast, any animal, and this small European deer is one.

clue.text: Rib position reinforced by Emergency Room

indicators.note: the hospital abbreviation goes inside, strengthening the word from within

parts.note: a line is a position, as a stance taken

explanation.surface: A broken rib being treated in a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rib' is the architectural sense, not the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gothic vaulting, a short tertiary rib linking the main ribs is this term.

clue.text: On board 12 interrupts progress from this routine

parts.words: On board 12 interrupts progress from this
parts.note: on a dartboard the 12 sits between the 9 and the 5, so 12 breaks up a run from one of those numbers to the other

explanation.surface: A board meeting cutting into the working day.
explanation.walkthrough: Around the rim of a dartboard the numbers run 9, 12, 5, so 12 interrupts a path from the first to the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Office hours of a standard working day, a fixed daily grind, are named for their start and finish times.

clue.text: 8 of South going after apprentice 8?

indicators.note: the letter follows the young trainee, coming after it in the answer

parts.note: a cub is a novice, as in cub reporter
8 across is OPPONENT; at the bridge table South's opponents are East and West, so E

explanation.surface: A bridge player's rival going after a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 8 is the number itself, not the entry; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is two multiplied by itself three times, so it is a perfect third power.

clue.text: Alternative to bottle party? It's possible

parts.note: drink comes in a can as well as a bottle
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Planning a bottle party and wondering if it will work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses a willing, positive attitude that a task is achievable.

clue.text: Boy soprano's nothing like this?

parts.note: a young choirboy's voice part, and the letter O (nothing) appears three times over in 'boy soprano'

explanation.surface: Someone claiming a choirboy is nothing like a certain voice type.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to deny a likeness, but the O in bOy sOprAnO occurs threefold.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest voice part sung by a boy chorister is named for being threefold, and the O appears three times.

clue.text: Unrestricted contract covers new fertility symbols

indicators.note: the trimmed contract word wraps around the letter for new
without its limits, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: an agreement is a contract

explanation.surface: An open-ended deal covering new emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrestricted' strips A and T from AGREEMENT to leave GREEMEN; 'covers' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliate heads carved in churches are pagan figures read as emblems of spring rebirth and fruitfulness.

clue.text: Cause to see red, initially, amber and green in new combination

indicators.note: the letters are put together in a new order
only the first letter of amber is used

explanation.surface: Traffic lights, red, amber and green, set in a new sequence to annoy drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes A from amber; 'in new combination' rearranges A plus GREEN. 'red' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become furious, so making someone do so is to infuriate them.

clue.text: Local game not the origin of pub brawls

indicators.note: the start of the word for pub is dropped

parts.note: a bar is a pub
rows are noisy quarrels or brawls

explanation.surface: A pub game that did not start the bar fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is the British word for one's neighbourhood pub; arrows is slang for darts.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is the classic pub pastime, and its players call the missiles, and the game, by this slang name.
